title: Jump Game II
prompt:
`nums[i]` is the max jump length from index `i`. Starting at index 0 (reaching the end is guaranteed), return the **minimum** number of jumps to reach the last index.

**Example**: `[2,3,1,1,4]` → `2` (index 0 → 1 → 4).

Greedy BFS by 'levels': each jump extends the farthest reachable frontier; count how many frontiers you cross.
hints: Track the current jump's reachable end (`curEnd`) and the farthest any index in it can reach (`farthest`).
When the scan hits `curEnd`, you must jump: increment jumps and set curEnd = farthest.
Loop only to n-2 (arriving at the last index needs no further jump).

solution.explanation: This is BFS layer-counting without a queue: everything reachable in k jumps forms one layer [previous end .. curEnd]. When the scan exhausts a layer, we've committed to a jump and extend to the farthest that layer could reach. O(n).
